transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for this afternoon's medication safety review of the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol, I'd like to hear from each of you before I sign off on the final decision. Pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical IT — please share any operational findings or concerns you've identified so far. I want to make sure we have all the information on the table before we determine what safeguards may be needed for the night shift.

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern from pharmacy. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. As a potential safeguard, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: From laboratory medicine, I have an important operational finding. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This is critical for the safety review because it affects how we'll be monitoring patients receiving the anticoagulant on the night shift.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: From nursing education, I have a critical staffing concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they are permitted to administer the medication. This is a significant safeguard consideration for the night shift, as it affects a large portion of the nursing staff who may be caring for patients on this protocol.

transcript.text: From clinical IT, I have an operational finding regarding the electronic medication record. I've confirmed that a high-priority alert can be deployed at 16:00 today, which will warn clinicians about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. This could serve as an additional safeguard alongside the other measures discussed, particularly given the selection errors pharmacy has already identified.

decisions.safety_protocol: Implement a temporary hold on the new IV anticoagulant protocol for the night shift, pending the medication safety review this afternoon. The protocol will not be used on the night shift until all safeguards are in place and signed off.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Remove both concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets. During the temporary hold, pharmacy will supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes, eliminating bedside selection between 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL concentrations.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Use aPTT testing every six hours as the approved replacement monitoring method until the anti-Xa analyzer is available for calibration on Friday at 17:00.
decisions.nurse_authorization: Require charge-nurse sign-off for any nurse who has not completed the new anticoagulant administration module before they are permitted to administer the medication. The 18 nurses on tonight's shift who have not completed the module must either complete it before the shift or receive charge-nurse sign-off.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority concentration selection alert at 16:00 today, requiring clinician acknowledgment before the order can be released, as an additional safeguard against selection errors.

commitments.detail: Remove both anticoagulant concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets and supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during the temporary hold.
Implement aPTT monitoring every six hours as the approved replacement until the anti-Xa analyzer is calibrated on Friday at 17:00.
Ensure charge-nurse sign-off is obtained for all 18 uncertified nurses before they administer the anticoagulant on the night shift.
Deploy the high-priority concentration selection alert at 16:00 today with mandatory acknowledgment before order release.
